We need to propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: a sulfonyl linking two phenyls, one side has methyl para to sulfonamide, other side has para-substituted with trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2? Actually the amide attaches to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N) meaning the amide nitrogen attached to phenyl with an NH at para? Wait: Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline with two amines? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline with an amine at position 1 and another amine at position? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N means an aniline with an amine attached to the aromatic carbon (the first N is attached to carbonyl, the second N is attached to the aromatic ring as substituent? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N": start N attached to carbonyl (C(=O)N...), then c3ccccc3N means the aromatic ring with an N attached at the end (an aniline). So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl which also has an amino substituent (aniline). So final product has three aromatic rings: ring A (methyl phenyl with sulfonamide), ring B (phenyl attached to sulfonyl, bearing trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2), ring C (aniline). So retrosynthesis steps: 1) disconnection of amide bond (C=O-N) to give carboxylic acid (trans-CH=CH-COOH) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). 2) disconnection of the alkene formation via Doebner modification: from aromatic aldehyde (maybe p-formyl phenyl sulfonyl) and malonic acid to give trans-CH=CH-COOH attached to phenyl sulfonyl. So break the C=C and C-COOH bond to give aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2 attached to sulfonyl) and malonic acid. 3) disconnection of sulfonamide: sulfonyl chloride reacting with aniline (the methyl phenyl amine). So break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph) and aniline (methyl phenyl amine). So three steps: amide formation, Doebner modification, sulfonamide formation.

We need to provide JSON route with three reaction nodes each with template_id (we need IDs). We haven't retrieved template IDs. We need to search for templates matching each transformation.

First step: amide formation from carboxylic acid and amine (coupling). Use functional_groups_broken: aliphatic carboxylic acid? Actually the acid is aliphatic (C=CH-COOH). So broken: aliphatic carboxylic acid. Formed: amide. Let's search again with correct functional group names: "aliphatic carboxylic acid" broken, "amide" formed. Already did, got empty. Maybe need to include "carboxylic esters"? But amide formation from acid is typical. Could be template exists but not returned due to limited catalog. Could try search with bonds broken/formed. For amide formation, bond broken: C-O (in acid), bond formed: C-N. Let's try.
